1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

The rain had been falling on Qingshi for three full days. Lin Xiaoyu shut the medicine shop door and lit the last lamp. She was twenty-two, and since her father's death she had run this small medicine shop alone.
"Is anyone there?" came a man's voice from outside.

Lin Xiaoyu hesitated a moment, then opened the door. A young man stood outside, soaked through, his left hand pressed to his right arm, blood seeping between his fingers. He said his name was Chen Ziming, and that he had come from the provincial capital.
"I need this bandaged," Chen Ziming said quietly. "I can pay. Is one hundred and twenty yuan enough?"

She didn't take his money, only had him sit by the counter while she turned to fetch gauze and medicinal wine. The wound wasn't deep, but it was long, as if it had been sliced open with a knife. As she cleaned it, she asked him how he'd been hurt.

Chen Ziming was silent for a long time before he said, "I ran into some men on the road. They wanted a letter I was carrying." He took an oil-paper packet from inside his coat and placed it on the table. "This letter must reach Baiyun before May 18."

Lin Xiaoyu glanced out the window. Baiyun was up on the mountain, forty li from Qingshi, and mountain roads were hardest in the rain. She remembered what her father always used to say: "If you save someone, see it through to the end."
"I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow," she said. "Tonight you can sleep in the back room."
2: Before dawn, Lin Xiaoyu woke Chen Ziming. She shouldered a bamboo basket packed with dried food, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella. Chen Ziming's arm had improved somewhat, but his face was still pale.
When they were halfway up the mountain, they ran into Zhou Dashan, an old man out gathering firewood. He recognized Lin Xiaoyu and asked with a smile where she was off to so early.
"Delivering medicine to Baiyun," Lin Xiaoyu replied. She made no mention of the letter.
Zhou Dashan glanced at Chen Ziming and lowered his voice. "Yesterday evening, three outsiders were asking around at the town entrance about an injured young man. You two be careful."

Chen Ziming's face went even paler. Lin Xiaoyu thanked the old man and led Chen Ziming away from the main road, onto a narrow trail known only to herb gatherers. The path was narrow and slippery; she walked in front, every step perfectly steady.

By noon, the rain had finally stopped. The mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the roof of Baiyun Temple in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate. Her name was Zhao Qiuyue, and she received guests at the temple.
Zhao Qiuyue took the oil-paper package, examined the red seal on the wrapper, and nodded. "The master has been waiting for this letter for 2 years," she said. "Thank you for your trouble."
On the way back, Chen Ziming said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come to Qingshi, help me fix the roof of my medicine shop."
